# Blackline 0.15.139

* The app's own appearance is the one Derek set: the cooler backdrop and teal accent as before, now
  with tighter corners, roomy spacing and no texture over the page. A device that never chose an
  appearance moves to it; one that chose keeps what it chose.
* Every emoji in the app is drawn from the same face. A picture is made once and kept for the
  session, and one made before the bundled Twemoji face had finished loading kept the system's own
  emoji — so one message drew a 3-D orange face and the next a flat one, for as long as the app was
  open. Nothing is drawn from the face until the face is there.
* Editing a message: the emoji button sits on the middle of a one-line box and at the end of a long
  one, the words stop before it, and the delivery tick no longer lands underneath it.
* The tick, or the clock, sits on the line when the message is one line and in the top corner when
  it is not — measured after the message is laid out, because a quote or a wrap makes a second line
  that the words themselves never show.
* A mention carries only a name. It used to print a piece of the person's address beside it and
  carry the whole of it in the tooltip, which in a space shows people an identity they were never
  given. A click still opens their card.
* A note is a box with lines in it: its words start inside it rather than pinned to its top edge.
* A call banner says what the call is doing: ringing, not reachable and it rings the moment they are
  back, connecting — and, when the ring is over and nobody came, that they declined or did not
  answer and you are sitting in this conversation's voice on your own.
* The name and the face you go by in a space are both set on your own row under Space settings →
  Members. The face had no control at all after the old menu item went, and the owner could not set
  either for themselves.
* A nickname typed on somebody's card shows on the card at once, rather than after you click away.
